obligations.note: The new route POST /payees/{id}/reopen maps to manage_payees, which is in rbac.PRIVILEGED, but is declared mfa=False in routes.py. The exhaustive control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails on exactly this route in the CI run on head.

The cited exception EXC-0183 (MFA-1, payments.routes, approved by risk owner Omar Haddad) expired on 2026-09-13, before the review time of 2026-10-16. No other exception in the register covers this deviation.

The CI run on head 331108b has result 'failure' (1 failure in 172 tests), so the full suite does not pass on the final commit. The required MFA-1 control test is the one that fails. Despite the description, no tests were changed.
Ledger entry ACR-0404 (MFA-1 evidence covering routes.py) lapses because routes.py changed in behaviour, and the replacement evidence of the same strength (the exhaustive route control test) fails.

The new state-changing operation reopen_payee calls _audit with actor, action 'reopen_payee' and target payee:{id}, as every state-changing method in service.py does. The sampled audit control test passes on head.
The new Store.reopen_payee only updates status and closed_at and writes no NPI fields. The exhaustive test test_every_npi_field_is_sealed_at_rest passes on head.
The new execute call uses a fixed SQL string with payee_id bound as a parameter. The exhaustive test test_sql_statements_are_parameterized passes on head.
Ticket CHG-24857 was approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-11, before review, and its components (payments.http, routes, service, store) cover all four touched files.
Code review approved by Mara Costa, a payments change_approver who is a different person from the author Aisha Bello.
Both approvals name the head commit 331108b, which is the only commit in the change.
The change touches security-sensitive components (routes, http, store). Security review approved by Kofi Mensah, a security_reviewer, on the head commit.

summary: The change adds POST /payees/{id}/reopen for the privileged manage_payees action without requiring MFA, which violates MFA-1. The only exception covering it, EXC-0183, expired on 2026-09-13, before the 2026-10-16 review, so it gives no cover under EXC-1. The change's own CI run on the final commit failed exactly on the MFA-1 control test, which contradicts the 'full suite green' claim and fails CHG-4, and the earlier MFA-1 ledger evidence has lapsed with no valid replacement. Ticketing, independent code review and security review are in order, but the violated obligations require rejection.
